questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit of a Function Involving the Special Limit With Sine
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that as $x\to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{3{sin}^{2}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}=1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{3{sin}^{2}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}{(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {[{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}]}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we can simplify the limit using trigonometric identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{4\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }÷4\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }÷\frac{4}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{4}) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{4}) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{({lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta })} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{4}=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡0}{4}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{4} & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we can simplify the limit using trigonometric identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}{3\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{3\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta })}{3\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{3\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{3{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{1}{3{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta } & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{1}{3{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }=\frac{1}{3{cos}^{4}⁡0}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta })\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{1}{3{cos}^{4}⁡\theta } & =1\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that as $x \to 0,$ both the numerator and denominator approach $0.$

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0}\: \dfrac{2\sin{x}}{3x} = \dfrac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form.

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 0}\: \dfrac{\sin{x}}{x} = 1
$$

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{3x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta }{4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta }{4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{1}{4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
\lim_\limits{\theta \to 0}\: \dfrac{\theta}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{({lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta })} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
\lim_\limits{\theta \to 0} \:\dfrac{1}{4 \cos \theta} = \dfrac{1}{4\cos 0} = \dfrac14.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{1}{4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
